Important nutrients for growth include protein, iron, calcium, vitamin C, vitamin D, and zinc. Calcium, in particular, has a key
role in bone development, and huge increments in bone density are seen during adolescence under the inﬂuence of sex hormones.
Bone density peaks in the early twenties and a low bone density at this time is related to an increased risk of osteoporosis in later life,
especially for women. Studies have suggested that body mass index (BMI) in adolescence is the best predictor of adult bone density,
explaining why children who experience anorexia nervosa are likely to have a higher risk of osteoporosis.
